{{Current events|year=2020|month=03|day=21|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Arts and culture
*[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United States]]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Tennessee]]
***The ''[[Grand Ole Opry]]'' broadcasts from an empty venue for the first time since 1925. [https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/wireStory/grand-ole-opry-play-empty-theater-69711372 (ABC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Socio-economic impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]
**[[Economy of China]], [[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic in mainland China]]
***[[China]] resumes construction of its infrastructure to help ease the economic impact of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/regional/2020/03/21/china-resumes-construction-of-nearly-90-of-infrastructure-projects (''The Star'')]
;Health and environment
*[[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] says at least 20 vaccines for [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] are in development around the world and that clinical trials are underway. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/over-20-vaccines-multiple-treatments-currently-in-development-for-coronavirus/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Asia]]
***[[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] reports zero domestic cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] for a third consecutive day. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/united-states-canada/article/3076237/coronavirus-latest-us-and-mexico-limit-travel (''South China Morning Post'')]
****[[China]] sends masks and medical experts abroad to aid countries affected by [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/china-virus-pr-offensive-sends-masks-experts-abroad-69723923 (ABC News)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in East Timor]]
****[[East Timor]] confirms its first case of [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2020/03/576783/east-timor-confirms-first-case-covid-19 (''New Strait Times'')]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] reports 18 imported cases of [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-taiwan-idUSKBN2180AU (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] confirms its second case of [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.fbcnews.com.fj/news/fiji-second-covid-19-cases-recorded/ (FBC News)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Africa]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Mauritius]]
****[[Mauritius]] reports its first death from [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-mauritius/mauritius-says-reports-first-death-from-coronavirus-idUSKBN2180GK?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Angola]]
****[[Angola]] reports its first confirmed cases of COVID-19, two male Angolan nationals who recently returned from [[Portugal]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-africa/angola-confirms-first-cases-as-coronavirus-spreads-in-africa-idUSKBN2180P4?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Uganda]]
****[[Uganda]] reports its first confirmed case of [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. The patient is a 36-year-old Ugandan male who recently arrived in the country on an [[Ethiopian Airlines]] flight from [[Dubai]]. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/health-pmn/uganda-says-has-confirmed-first-coronavirus-case (''National Post'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Europe]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] says an additional 793 people have died from [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in the country, bringing the death toll to 4,825. It is the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date. [https://nypost.com/2020/03/21/italys-coronavirus-death-toll-spikes-by-nearly-800-in-one-day/ (''New York Post'')]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Finland]]
****[[Finland]]'s [[National Institute for Health and Welfare (Finland)|National Institute for Health and Welfare]] reports the country's first death from [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://yle.fi/uutiset/osasto/news/coronavirus_latest_first_death_521_confirmed_cases_in_finland_pupils_in_grades_1-3_can_return_to_school/11249610 (Yle)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Georgia (country)]]
****[[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] declares a nationwide state of emergency due to [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], effective until April 21. [https://civil.ge/archives/342486 (Civil Georgia)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Spain)|Ministry of Health]] reports an additional 324 [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] deaths, the country's largest one-day increase. The country's death toll stands at 1,326, with 24,926 cases, the second highest in [[Europe]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/coronavirus-spain-death-toll-cases-rise-latest-a9415831.html (''The Independent'')]
****[[Spain]] announces it is closing hotels in the country for the sake of converting them into hospitals, as local medical facilities are being overwhelmed by [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] patients. A [[military hospital]] will also be constructed in the capital [[Madrid]]. [https://origin.lailasnews.com/spain-orders-hotels-to-close-starts-converting-them-into-hospitals-as-coronavirus-death-toll-rises/ (Lailasnews)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-spain/spain-to-treat-thousands-of-coronavirus-patients-in-conference-hall-as-toll-tops-1000-idUSKBN2172KO (Reuters)]
****[[Lorenzo Sanz]], the former president of [[Real Madrid CF]], dies after testing positive for [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/realmadrid/real-madrid-president-lorenzo-sanz-dies-dead-coronavirus-a4394076.html (''Evening Standard'')]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] orders all pubs, restaurants, theaters, cinemas, gyms and other social hubs to close down to prevent the spread of the [[coronavirus disease 2019|coronavirus]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-britain-cafes/the-united-kingdom-is-closed-johnson-shutters-pubs-and-restaurants-idUKKBN2172VY (Reuters)]
****The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Department of Health and Social Care]] confirms 53 more deaths from [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], bringing the country's death toll to 233. All those who died had underlying health conditions and the oldest patient was 94-years-old, according to [[NHS England]]. [https://www.itv.com/news/2020-03-21/uk-death-toll-reaches-233-as-a-further-53-die-after-testing-positive-for-coronavirus/ (''ITV News'')]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Albania]]
****[[Albania]]'s government deploys [[Albanian Land Force|troops]] to enforce a 40-hour nationwide [[curfew]]. [[Prime Minister of Albania|Prime Minister]] [[Edi Rama]] says Albanians "will stay inside after 13:00", and that police and the armed forces "will use force against whoever breaks the law, including pensioners, and will use water canons and tear gas if need be." [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-albania/albania-deploys-troops-to-enforce-40-hour-coronavirus-curfew-idUSKBN2180NW?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports 112 more deaths from [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], bringing the country's death toll to 562. There are 1,525 people in severe condition with the virus, half of which are people under the age of 60. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200321-france-records-112-coronavirus-deaths-in-a-day-as-death-toll-reaches-562 (France 24)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]]'s [[Ministry of the Interior (Turkey)|Ministry of the Interior]] imposes a [[curfew]] for people over the age of 65 and the [[Chronic condition|chronically ill]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkey-announces-curfew-for-elderly-chronically-ill/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
****[[Turkey]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Turkey)|Ministry of Health]] reports that the country's [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] death toll stands at 21, with 947 confirmed cases. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/covid-19-cases-in-turkey-rise-to-947-deaths-to-21/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in North America]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United States]]
****[[Ketchikan, Alaska|Ketchikan]], in [[Southeast Alaska|Southeast]] [[Alaska]], shelters in place after six people test positive for [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in the town of 8,000 residents. [https://www.ktuu.com/content/news/3-new-COVID-19-cases-causes-a-shelter-in-place-proclamation-for-Ketchikan-569001431.html (KTUU-TV)]
****[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] says eight people have died from [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.mlive.com/news/2020/03/8-people-now-dead-from-coronavirus-in-michigan-infant-tests-positive.html (MLive)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in South America]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Chile]]
****[[Chile]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Chile)|Ministry of Health]] reports its country's first [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] death in an 83-year woman from [[Renca]], [[Santiago, Chile|Santiago]]. The country has more than 500 confirmed cases, the second-largest number in [[South America]] after [[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Brazil|Brazil]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-chile/chile-health-minister-confirms-first-death-due-to-coronavirus-idUSKBN2180WL (Reuters)] 
;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]], [[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction]]
**[[Yonhap News Agency]] reports that [[North Korea]] has fired two projectiles from [[Pyongan Province]] into the [[Sea of Japan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-missiles-idUSKBN2173MB (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-51984344 (BBC News)]
*[[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[North Korea]] says that [[United States|U.S.]] [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] wrote a letter to [[List of leaders of North Korea#Supreme Leader of the DPRK|Supreme Leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] to express his willingness to work with him on dealing with [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-usa-northkorea-idUSKBN2180YX (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
**[[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]] and his wife [[Karen Pence]] test negative for [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/21/coronavirus-pence-says-he-will-be-tested-after-staff-member-diagnosis.html (CNBC)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic on sports]]
**[[Football player]] [[Wu Lei]], a [[China|Chinese]] national based in [[Spain]], tests positive for [[coronavirus disease 2019|COVD-19]]. He says he is recovering from the virus. [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-soccer-china-idUKKBN2180OX (Reuters)]
